title: Floating Roof Tank

introduction.definition: An external floating roof tank stores volatile liquids like crude oil. The roof floats on the liquid and moves up and down with the level, so there is almost no vapour space — cutting evaporation losses and fire risk. A rim seal closes the gap to the shell; a rolling ladder follows the roof.
key_points: Legs support the roof at low level

video_tutorials.title: Floating Roof Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Floating Roof Tank.
An external floating roof tank stores volatile liquids like crude oil.
The roof floats on the liquid and moves up and down with the level, so there is almost no vapour space — cutting evaporation losses and fire risk.
A rim seal closes the gap to the shell; a rolling ladder follows the roof.
Typical applications include crude oil and gasoline storage; refinery and terminal storage; volatile intermediates.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Floating Roof Tank works.
Product enters through the inlet nozzle and the level rises.

video_tutorials.title: Floating Roof Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Floating Roof Tank.
Check roof position and drain.
Inspect rim seals and pontoons.
Out-of-service inspection (API 653).
Watch for roof sinking: roof tilts or sinks. Common cause: rainwater not drained, pontoon leaks.
Watch for rim seal fire / emissions: odour, fire. Common cause: damaged seal.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
